content:
Let \(x_1,x_2,x_3,\dots\) be the counts of \(7,77,777,\dots\).

Digit count equation:
\[
x_1+2x_2+3x_3+\cdots=19
\]
Value equation:
\[
7x_1+77x_2+777x_3+\cdots=2023
\]
Divide the value equation by \(7\):
\[
x_1+11x_2+111x_3+\cdots=289
\]
Subtract the digit equation:
\[
9x_2+108x_3+\cdots=270
\]
\[
x_2+12x_3+123x_4+\cdots=30
\]
Only \(x_2,x_3\) can be nonzero because larger coefficients exceed \(30\). Thus:
\[
x_2+12x_3=30
\]
Substitute into the digit equation:
\[
x_1+2x_2+3x_3=19
\]
From \(x_2=30-12x_3\):
\[
x_1+2(30-12x_3)+3x_3=19
\]
\[
x_1=21x_3-41
\]
Since \(x_1\ge0\) and \(x_3\) is integer, \(x_3=2\). Then:
\[
x_2=30-12(2)=6
\]

\[
\boxed{6}
\]
